site.title: ellipog
site.description: Manuals for Tenet, Armature and Stature, Minecraft mods for Fabric and NeoForge: how they work, how to configure them, and what the file formats are.

/*sponsor: One affiliate arrangement, in the manifest because that is where the site's facts live — a link and a discount code written into a component would be a second place to keep in step. `code` is quoted verbatim on the page, and `url` carries the referral path.

sponsor.name: Shockbyte

badge.label: Hosting partner
badge.note: Ellipog is a Shockbyte partner, paid a commission on what is bought through this link.

sponsor./*badge: The small mark beside the host's name. `label` is what shows; `note` is the full phrase in the native tooltip, for a reader who wants to know what the mark means. The label is `Hosting partner`, and it was `Partner` alone until it was read beside the tagline it qualifies: `Minecraft server hosting` next to `PARTNER` says what the host does and that there is some arrangement, but not what the arrangement is about -- partner *of what*? `Hosting partner` carries both halves, so the chip states the relationship rather than leaving the tagline to imply it. Two alternatives were considered and dropped, and both are recorded here so they are not re-proposed: `Infrastructure` names a category this arrangement is not, and `Verified`/`Verified partner` claims a status the host does not confer -- Shockbyte's own material says `partner`, `Partner Program` and `affiliate link`, and never `verified`, so that word would be inventing a status, and a trust mark that overstates is worse than none. Change `label` to change the wording; nothing else needs touching.
sponsor./*logo: One mark, not two: the glyph takes its ink from `currentColor`, so one file works on either ground. Generated by `bun run brand` from design/brand-source/shockbyte-flat.svg, the single-colour wordmark in Shockbyte's own branding kit (which ships it in dark and in white, so a one-colour mark is theirs rather than a recolour), and committed like the mod icons. Inlined by `BrandMark`, like the tip jar's. There is no full-colour `logoColor` plate any more: that existed because the previous host's brand rules forbade a monochrome version, and Shockbyte's do not. **This path is what `BrandMark` reads**, so the manifest is the one place it is written.
sponsor./*logoSize: The mark declares a viewBox of 1019.2 by 222 and no width or height of its own, so these are the numbers the layout reserves before it is parsed. They match the viewBox ratio (129 / 28 = 4.6), and 28 is the height `.brand-mark` draws every mark at. `BrandMark` derives the width from them rather than the other way round.

/*support: The second cell in the band at the foot of every page: Ko-fi, where the mods' own running costs are tipped into. It is NOT a sponsorship and nothing about it is paid for -- so it carries no `rel="sponsored"`, no `Affiliate link` note, no badge, and its own landmark rather than the host's, because a region labelled `Sponsored` that also holds an unpaid tip jar is the misattribution the disclosure exists to prevent. `tagline` is what shows under the mark, and the handle beside it is derived from `url` rather than typed next to it, so the two cannot disagree. `logo`, `logoWidth` and `logoHeight` are the mark: the box it is drawn in, which `BrandMark` reads rather than being told, so `check.mjs` can hold the rendered box to these numbers. Deleting this object deletes the cell and the row falls back to one full-width cell.

support.name: Ko-fi
support./*logo: Generated by `bun run brand` from design/brand-source/kofi.svg -- Ko-fi's own wordmark, committed verbatim from their brand asset pack. Three quirks of that file are handled in the transform rather than by editing the source, and one of them is a dark-mode bug: its capsule and letterforms are the named colour `white`, which is this site's *ground*, so left named it renders as a white slab on a dark page while looking correct on a light one.
support./*logoSize: 124 by 34. The ratio is the file's (738 by 202, rounded to the pixel). These two numbers are the box `BrandMark` reserves and the ratio it derives the width from, so the size is one edit and the page cannot drift from it.

/*studio: Who engineers and maintains this site, and the one thing the colophon row at the foot of every page says. It is here rather than in the component for the same reason the sponsor is: the wording is a site fact, so changing it is one edit and the page cannot drift from it. `label` is quoted verbatim; `url` is the link AND the domain shown beside it, derived rather than typed twice, so the two cannot disagree.

author.bio: I build Minecraft mods. A few are in development now; the rest are already out.

/*suite: ONLY MODS THAT EXIST. Every entry here is `status: "active"`, and `app/page.tsx` renders an entry only when it is -- so a mod is named on the site the day it is certain to ship and not before. A planned mod is not listed, not summarised, and not named anywhere in this repository: the idea is the thing being kept private, and a name plus a one-line summary is enough of it to be worth keeping. Those entries live in `design/planned/suite.json`, which is gitignored, and they move in here when the mod is certain. `check.mjs` asserts both halves of this -- that no entry is anything but active, and that the catalog says `planned` nowhere.

suite.name: Tenet
suite.summary: A questing engine that ships no questlines of its own. JSON files in, a pannable canvas out, and the server, not the client, decides what counts as done. Parties share progress, and an in-game editor with undo writes the same files the manual describes.
suite./*versions: One entry per documented game version, latest first. The top-level pin/minecraft/loaders above always describe the default (latest) version, so every existing reader keeps working. `branch` is the git branch the pin tracks, read by `bun run pins`; `localPath` names the sibling checkout and is only set on the version under active development, so any other version always builds from its pin, even on a machine with the repositories beside it. Unversioned URLs (`/docs/tenet/...`) always show the default version; older ones live under `/docs/tenet/<id>/...`. No version is ever dropped for being close to another: the whole tree is kept.

suite.name: Armature
suite.summary: A shared library mod. One loader seam, event, network, energy and team APIs, a strict JSON reader, and a client UI toolkit for layout, text, shapes, themes and widgets: all drawn through one game-free renderer seam, and nothing in it specific to any one consumer.
